Sri Manas Kumar Mondal vs The State Of West Bengal And
Others on 2 February, 2026

Author: Hiranmay Bhattacharyya
Bench: Hiranmay Bhattacharyya
 A. 12
02.02.2026
 Court No.19
 Bp
 Wpa 28144 of 2025
 Sri Manas Kumar Mondal
 -versus-
 The State of West Bengal and others
 Mr. Dhiman Ray
 Mr. Pritam Modak
 Mr. Dip Chanda
 ..for the petitioner
 Mr. Jyoti Prakash Chatterjee
 Mr. Arindam Mitra
 ..for the State
 Mr. Ashok Kumar Jena
 ..for the respondent no.8

The petitioner claims to be the owner of several plots of land within Mouza Mathureshchak, J.L. No.
205 under Police Station Haldia, District Purba Medinipur as specifically mentioned in paragraph 2 of the writ petition.

entities.text: Police Station Haldia, District Purba Medinipur
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The grievance of the petitioner is that in spite of an application being filed under the provisions of Right to Information Act, no effective information has been supplied to the petitioner in respect of the aforesaid plots of land.

Mr. Jena, learned advocate appearing for the respondent no.8 supplies a letter dated 9th December,
2025 and submits that the said letter was issued to the learned advocate on record of the petitioner furnishing the necessary information.

By referring to the said information Mr. Jena submits that all the plots as referred to in paragraph 2 of the writ petition was subject matter of two acquisition proceedings one being L.A. Case No. 20/62-63 and the other being L.A. 11/63-64.
He further submits that the lands were acquired and handed over to the Shyama Prosad Mookerjee Port, Kolkta on 24th June, 1963 and 24th March, 1965 respectively.
Mr. Chatterjee, learned advocate appears for the State.
He submits that the plots referred to in paragraph 2 of the writ petition were acquired in accordance with law and compensation amount has also been paid.

sentences.text: The primary grievance as it appears from the writ petition was that the petitioner was not aware as to whether the plots mentioned in paragraph 2 of the writ petition was subject matter of any acquisition proceeding or not.
In view of the reply given under the provisions of the Right to Information Act, nothing survives to be decided in the instant writ petition.
Accordingly, WPA 28144 of 2025 stands disposed of leaving the petitioner free to take appropriate steps in accordance with law.
There shall be however no order as to costs.

Urgent certified photocopy of this order, if applied for,
be supplied to the parties expeditiously on compliance of usual legal formalities.

(Hiranmay Bhattacharyya, J.)
